 "Applies fn f to the argument list formed by prepending intervening arguments to args."
 (fn ([f args]
   (let [n (suss.bootstrap/vector-count args)]
     (if (and (not (suss.bootstrap/nil? n)) (<= n 4))
     (cond (== n 0) (f) (== n 1) (f (nth args 0)) (== n 2) (f (nth args 0) (nth args 1)) (== n 3) (f (nth args 0) (nth args 1) (nth args 2)) :else (f (nth args 0) (nth args 1) (nth args 2) (nth args 3)))
     (if (and (not (suss.bootstrap/fixed-arity-fn? f)) (.-cljs$lang$applyTo f))
     (let [fixed-arity (.-cljs$lang$maxFixedArity f)
           bc (bounded-count (inc fixed-arity) args)]
       (if (<= bc fixed-arity)

     (let [bc (bounded-count 21 args)]
       (if (<= bc 20) (apply-to f bc args) (apply-to-simple f (seq args))))))))

rationale: Retain every pinned source apply branch and signature with explicit defn bootstrap. Bounded reproducible apply generators preserve the complete arity ladder and source-array fallback; compiler-owned closures supply rooted arity properties and sequence-preserving applyTo. Full compiled macro/bootstrap and namespace warning acceptance remain unfinished. A PersistentVector of up to four elements as the last argument is spread positionally, as the call (f x … (nth args 0) …) that apply computes, with no arglist or arity properties (#445). A function without cljs$lang$applyTo, one with fixed arities only or a non-fn callable, is called through apply-to with up to twenty arguments, counted as Clojure's AFn.applyToHelper counts them, rather than through apply-to-simple's arity property reads (#466). A fn whose arities are all fixed, as suss.bootstrap/fixed-arity-fn? reads from its code, has no applyTo and skips that property's read.
